name.text: 16.1 Q3 Horizontal line test on an Eldoret sacco fare curve

questiontext.text:
A matatu sacco in Eldoret charges a fare that depends on the distance travelled. The manager wants to know whether two different distances ever give exactly the same fare. The board shows the fare curve, with distance on the horizontal axis and fare on the vertical axis, and a red horizontal line that you can move with the slider.

Slide the line through the whole height of the graph. If some horizontal line meets the curve at two or more points, then two different distances give the same fare.

[[jsxgraph width="400px" height="300px"]] (function() { var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [-1, 8, 10, -1.2], axis: true, grid: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false}); var o = {#one2one#}; var fare = function(x) { if (o == 1) { return 0.6*x + 0.5; } // rises, then a flat fare zone from 3 km to 6 km, then rises again if (x < 3) { return 0.6*x + 0.5; } if (x < 6) { return 2.3; } return 0.6*(x - 6) + 2.3; }; b.create('functiongraph', [fare, 0, 9], {strokeColor: '#1565c0', strokeWidth: 2}); var hy = b.create('slider', [[4.2, 7.3], [7.5, 7.3], [0, 3, 7]], {name: 'y', snapWidth: 0.1}); b.create('line', [[-1, function() { return hy.Value(); }], [10, function() { return hy.Value(); }]], {strokeColor: '#c62828', strokeWidth: 2, dash: 2, fixed: true}); b.create('text', [8.3, -0.6, 'distance'], {fontSize: 11, fixed: true}); b.create('text', [0.2, 7.6, 'fare'], {fontSize: 11, fixed: true}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

Is this fare function one-to-one or many-to-one?

The fare function is [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The horizontal line test says that a function is one-to-one when no horizontal line meets its graph more than once. A horizontal line fixes one output; two or more crossings mean that different inputs share that output, so the function is many-to-one. One crossing is expected and is not a problem.

[[if test="is(one2one=1)"]]

Here the fare rises steadily with distance. Every horizontal line meets the graph at most once, so no two distances give the same fare. The fare function is one-to-one.

[[else]]

Here the fare rises, stays flat between 3 km and 6 km, then rises again. The horizontal line at the height of the flat part meets the graph at every distance from 3 km to 6 km, so many different distances give the same fare. The fare function is many-to-one.

[[/if]]

questiondescription.text: This question is based on the definitions of one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many relations in Section 16.1 (Types of Relations) of the Grade 11 Functions topic.

node.description: Correct conclusion from the horizontal line test?

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(one2one=0)"]]

It looks like you judged from the general upward shape rather than testing with the line. A fare curve that rises can still level off and repeat a fare. Drag the horizontal line through the whole height of the graph and look for a height where it meets the curve more than once.

[[else]]

Remember that a single crossing is expected and is fine. The test looks for two or more crossings at the same height. Drag the horizontal line through the whole height of the graph and check whether any height is reached twice.

[[/if]]
